3. A force of $10\text{ N}$ acts on a stationary object of mass $10\text{ kg}$. After $10\text{ s}$ a force of $20\text{ N}$ acts on it for $5\text{ s}$ in the opposite direction. What is the distance traveled by the object?

4. You have jumped from a boat with a velocity of $10\text{ m/s}$ towards the bank. Your mass and the mass of the boat are $50\text{ kg}$ and $100\text{ kg}$ respectively. In which direction and with what velocity will the boat move?

5. The coefficient of friction $\mu$ of a wooden piece on a floor is $0.01$. If the mass of the wooden piece is $10\text{ kg}$, what is the force required in moving it? If a stone of mass $100\text{ kg}$ is kept on the wooden block, what is force required to move it? What happens if the floor is frictionless?

Put the tick ($\sqrt{_{\quad}}$) mark on the correct answer

1. The tendency or property of a body to maintain its present state for ever is called:
(a) force
(b) acceleration
(c) inertia
(d) velocity

2. Which one is the dimension of force?
(a) $MLT^{-2}$
(b) $MLT^{-1}$
(c) $ML^{-2}T^{-2}$
(d) $M^{-1}LT^{-2}$

3. Which one is the unit of momentum?
(a) $\text{kg m}$
(b) $\text{kg ms}^{-1}$
(c) $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$
(d) $\text{kg ms}^{-2}$

4. A force of $50\text{ N}$ is applied on a body of mass $5\text{ kg}$, its acceleration will be-
(a) $12\text{ ms}^{-2}$
(b) $8\text{ ms}^{-2}$
(c) $13\text{ ms}^{-2}$
(d) $10\text{ ms}^{-2}$

5. If a mass of $10\text{ kg}$ moves with a velocity of $10\text{ ms}^{-1}$, its momentum will be-
(a) $10\text{ kg ms}^{-1}$
(b) $120\text{ kg ms}^{-1}$
(c) $100\text{ kg ms}^{-1}$
(d) $1\text{ kg ms}^{-1}$
